name: Fraunhofer n-type silicon solar cell with a tunnel oxide passivated contact
description: Fraunhofer ISE reported a 24%-efficient n-type silicon solar cell whose full-area rear contact used a thin silicon layer and a tunnel oxide to limit carrier recombination while conducting charge.

date.label: By 27 November 2013
date.basis: The institute’s dated release reports a cell result already achieved.

events.statement: Fraunhofer ISE reported 24% conversion efficiency for a laboratory n-type silicon cell with a tunnel oxide passivated contact covering its rear surface.
events.place_note: Fraunhofer ISE, Freiburg im Breisgau, Germany.
events.scope: The research cell announced in November. The paper presented in Paris earlier in 2013 addresses the same contact concept.

evidence.locator: pp. 1–2, description of the cell and research support
evidence.supports: Reports the 24% result, continuous rear contact, location and federal research support.

earliest_record.rationale: The institute’s announcement establishes an upper bound on this prototype’s 24% result.

why: The research group targeted recombination losses at rear contacts and resistance losses from longer carrier paths in partial-contact structures. The German Federal Ministry for the Environment, Nature Conservation and Nuclear Safety supported the contact research.
